cases.title: Gary Glitter (Paul Gadd) — UK, Cambodia and Vietnam cases
cases.who: Paul Gadd ('Gary Glitter', pop singer)
cases.what: Convicted in the UK in 1999 of possessing thousands of child abuse images (about 4,000; jailed four months). He was expelled from Cambodia in 2002 amid sex-crime allegations. In March 2006 a Vietnamese court convicted him of obscene acts with two girls aged 10 and 11; he spent about two and a half years in jail there. In February 2015, after Operation Yewtree, he was convicted of attempted rape, four indecent assaults and one count of sex with a girl under 13, against three girls in 1975–1980, and sentenced to 16 years. Released in February 2023, he was recalled to prison in March 2023 for breaching licence conditions.

cases.title: Belgium (Flanders) — expert panel and Ethiopia investigation on intercountry adoption malpractice
cases.who: Flemish adoption services; intermediaries in Ethiopia and other countries of origin
cases.what: After reports of malpractice in adoptions from Ethiopia in 2019, the Flemish government appointed an independent expert panel on intercountry adoption, which delivered its findings in 2021 (final report dated 15 February 2023), and funded the Flemish Centre for Adoption to examine Ethiopian adoptions from 1997 to 2015. Preliminary conclusions found that the true story sometimes differed from the adoption files and that in the worst cases children had not been given up voluntarily by their birth parents. The panel's report led to screening of every country of origin, after which Flanders stopped adoptions from Vietnam and then from Gambia, Haiti and Morocco.

cases.title: Norway — NOU 2026:7 finds illegal and unethical intercountry adoptions
cases.who: Norwegian adoption organisations; Norwegian authorities; partner orphanages and bodies in 12 countries
cases.what: A government committee appointed in 2023 presented NOU 2026:7 'Forsvarlighet, risiko og tillit' on 22 June 2026. Examining adoptions from 12 countries since the 1950s, it concluded there were illegal or unethical conditions and that the Norwegian adoption system had clear shortcomings throughout the period. Individual findings included a kidnapped child adopted to Norway, a mother told she would get money if she consented, and documents deliberately falsified; payments to orphanages or organisations were sometimes linked to the number of children adopted.
cases.cover_up: Organisations did not always tell Norwegian authorities about payments or errors; authorities kept approving adoptions after learning of risks and illegalities.

cases.title: UK — 5,999 child potential victims referred to the National Referral Mechanism (2024)
cases.who: Home Office (NRM)
cases.what: Home Office statistics show 19,125 potential victims of modern slavery referred in 2024, 31 per cent (5,999) children; 78 per cent of child referrals were boys and criminal exploitation was the most common type (48 per cent). UK nationals were 23 per cent of all referrals, three-quarters of them children; Vietnamese nationals were 11 per cent, 416 of them children. In 2017 the Times reported more than 150 Vietnamese minors had gone missing from UK care since 2015.

cases.title: Vietnam — Nam Dinh ring: 266 babies sold for foreign adoption
cases.who: Heads of two provincial social welfare centres; doctors and nurses at village clinics
cases.what: In September 2009 a court in Nam Dinh tried 16 people, including the head of two social welfare centres and village clinic doctors and nurses, for 'abuse of power and authority'. They allegedly solicited infants from poor families and falsified documents saying the babies were abandoned; 266 babies were sent for foreign adoption from 2005 to July 2008. In April 2008 the US embassy in Hanoi had reported desertion numbers rising 17-fold or more at orphanages in 7 provinces, and Vietnam did not renew its adoption agreement with the US when it expired in September 2008.

cases.title: Thailand — 'Baby 101' surrogate baby-breeding operation
cases.who: Baby 101 company
cases.what: In February 2011 Thai police freed 14 Vietnamese women, half of them pregnant, held in two Bangkok houses with passports confiscated by a company called Baby 101 that took orders from childless couples for newborns. A Taiwanese woman said to run the operation was charged with human trafficking; four said they had been tricked, and the health minister said some appeared to have been raped.

cases.title: Vietnam and Laos → China — girls sold as brides (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Traffickers and marriage brokers
cases.what: The 2025 US TIP reports say traffickers in Vietnamese border villages lure women and girls, particularly Hmong, to China for forced marriages involving sex trafficking or forced labour, and use 'bride kidnapping' to exploit ethnic-minority girls in the northwest highlands; in Laos, traffickers increasingly kidnap or recruit women and girls via marriage brokers to China for sex trafficking, forced labour and forced surrogacy. Vietnam identified 236 child victims in 2024.
